name: Lin Health
founded_year_range: 2021 (stated in company press releases Oct 2024 and Dec 2025; Trustpilot profile claimed Dec 2021)
category: digital app/platform (virtual physician-led, coach-delivered pain practice)
cost_summary: Usually billed to insurance at a copay. Self-pay plans as of Oct 2026: Intensive $269/mo (4 live 30-min sessions/mo; list $378) or Core $159/mo (2 sessions/mo; list $189). Commitment plans: $129/mo month-to-month (first month $99), $109/mo billed per 6 months, or $984/yr. HSA/FSA eligible. Free mini-course and webinars at rethinkpain.lin.health. A reported 33% Mayo-referral discount was not re-verified.
mechanisms: neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
mechanism_summary: Lin's model is "brain-first." Most chronic pain is treated as ICD-11 chronic primary pain: an over-sensitised pain-signalling system misreads safe signals as danger (the PRT model). Fear of movement and worry keep it going (TSK-11 is tracked as a mediator), and stress or unprocessed emotion amplifies it (the EAET influence). A physician triage separates primary pain from structural pain (white-paper figures: 70% primary only, 26% mixed, 4% structural). The same model is applied to every listed condition, including POTS, CFS, IBS, hives and tinnitus.
techniques: Pain Reprocessing Therapy (pain neuroscience education, evidence lists, somatic tracking, safety reappraisal)
Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy elements
live 1:1 pain-recovery coaching (30 min, 2-4/mo) plus in-app messaging
physician medical review and triage (primary vs structural pain)
app lessons and care kits, symptom tracking
PT and psychiatry input as needed
mainstream_notes: Verified: Mayo Clinic is an investor and collaborator (press release Oct 22 2024). Lin provides post-discharge care for Mayo Rochester's Fibromyalgia Treatment Program, with planned expansion to Mayo Arizona primary care. Also verified: Anthem BCBS Maine statewide network from Mar 20 2023, with an in-person site in Portland, ME. Company-reported but not re-verified: BCBS Minnesota network, WellSpan and Lowell Pain Center/Tufts referral partnerships, and the 2024 HLTH Digital Health Hub Rising Star award. There is no guideline, NICE or CMS endorsement specific to Lin.
insurance_notes: Lin bills as an in-network specialty practice. Payers named in the Oct 2024 release: Aetna, Anthem BCBS, BCBS TX, Cigna, Harvard Pilgrim, Humana, Medicare, UnitedHealthcare. The company reports 27M covered lives (Oct 2024) and 60M (Dec 2025). The pricing FAQ still lists in-network coverage only in TX, CO and ME, so coverage varies by state and plan. HSA/FSA eligible.

key_trials.citation: Lin Health Medical Group white paper, June 2023 (not peer-reviewed)
key_trials.finding: 76% doing better at 3-6 months; 45% reduction in pain intensity; elevated fear of movement fell from 57% to 13%; NPS 60. Many data points missing; no control group.

key_trials.citation: Ashar YK, Gordon A, Schubiner H, et al. JAMA Psychiatry 2022;79(1):13-23 (PMID 34586357). Related technique (PRT), not the Lin program; first author Ashar disclosed personal fees from Lin Health
key_trials.design: RCT: PRT vs open-label placebo injection vs usual care, chronic back pain
key_trials.finding: 66% pain-free or nearly pain-free after PRT vs 20% placebo and 10% usual care; largely maintained at 1 year. 5-year follow-up: JAMA Psychiatry 2025;82(10):1049-51 (PMID 40736996).

key_trials.citation: Sturgeon J, Trost Z, Ashar YK, Lumley MA, Schubiner H, Clauw D, Hassett AL. Reg Anesth Pain Med 2025 (PMID 40973446). Related technique, not Lin; Ashar is a Lin consultant
key_trials.design: Single-arm open-label pilot of 3-session telehealth Brief PRT for fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: 33/35 completed; acceptability high. Completers showed reduced pain intensity (3-month d=0.89), interference (d=1.06) and pain-related fear (d=1.04); 42.3% much or very much improved at 3 months. No control group.

controversy: Headline outcome statistics come from uncontrolled self-report or are borrowed from the PRT RCT (92%, 98%, 76%, 45%, 47%), and some pages show placeholder figures. A back-pain evidence base is extended to POTS, CFS, hives, tinnitus, GERD and "pseudoseizures." Care is coach-delivered rather than therapist-delivered, which has not been tested. No peer-reviewed trial of Lin itself was found in PubMed (Oct 2026). The first author of the pivotal PRT trial (Ashar) is a paid Lin consultant and advisor, and Mayo Clinic is both investor and collaborator with a disclosed financial interest. The general ME/CFS-community critique of brain-based models also applies.

indicators.value: $15.4M by Oct 2024; +$11M Series A Dec 2025 (Proofpoint Capital lead)
Consumer Wellness Rising Star, Digital Health Hub Foundation at HLTH (not re-verified)

popularity.reach_estimate: ~10,000-30,000 treated patients cumulatively. Basis: ~1,000 in 8 months by early 2023, payer coverage growing to 60M lives, and the >1M interventions figure (message- and session-level). Free content reaches more people.
popularity.method_notes: Trajectory is anchored on company milestones: founding 2021; all-50-states telehealth and advisors 2022; Anthem Maine and the white paper (1,045 patients) 2023; $5.2M round, Mayo collaboration, 27M lives and the HLTH award 2024; $11M Series A and 60M lives 2025; Trustpilot review velocity of 165 per year in 2026. Web-search budget limits meant Reddit, Google Trends and Wayback were not checked. Reach is an order-of-magnitude estimate from the white-paper cohort size scaled by funding and coverage growth.
